newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca seen posting strong H1 despite stg.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca seen posting strong H1 despite stg.

text.p: British drugs and speciality chemicals company Zeneca Group Plc is expected to post a strong set of first-half results on August 7, benefiting from its currency hedging policy and a robust performance by major products.

Zeneca is expected to announce first-half, pre-tax profits of between 623 and 670 million stg, compared with 610 million stg a year earlier. The dividend is seen rising to between 13.0 pence and 13.7 pence from 12.5 pence per share.

The median pre-tax profit forecast of 649 million stg would represent a gain of more than six percent in headline profits, in line with British-based rival SmithKline Beecham Plc and in stark contrast to the 2.2 percent fall announced on Thursday by Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
Analysts said Zeneca's hedging policy had protected it from some of the ravages of the rising pound over the past year.
"I think this will be a good set of figures," said Merrill Lynch analyst Nigel Barnes, who expects pre-tax profit of 650 million stg.
However, Barnes said the group's top-selling heart drug, Zestril, was likely to see a retreat in sales in the first half as the comparative 1996 period was particularly strong.

With talk of a bid for the company waning in recent months, managers will be happy to focus on the progress of new products. A raft of launches and pending approvals has led to a rise in expenditure, putting some pressure on margins.

Asthma pill Accolate, which caused a stir last week after the FDA advised Zeneca to change labelling on the drug, is expected to have made rapid progress in the U.S. market, where it is competing with inhaled products.

It may be too early to assess the performance of Zeneca's new migraine drug Zomig, launched recently in the UK. However, any indication of its progress would be of great interest, not least to Glaxo, a major player in migraine which licensed Zomig to Zeneca as a condition of its merger with Wellcome.
"It will be worth watching Glaxo shares if the news on Zomig is good," an analyst with a UK brokerage said.

The results will also give the first clear picture of the performance of the group's new multi-purpose fungicide Amistar, which Zeneca management believes is one of the group's most-promising products.
Amistar has been launched in Germany and has won approvals for some uses in the U.S.
There has been speculation that Zeneca could announce a share split to take into account its surging stock price, which broke through the 20 stg barrier last month.
